general.summary: Generic call flow that works for any product. Use as scaffolding; pull in hub-specific lines from the per-hub scripts below.
general.opener: Hi, this is [Your name] calling from [Brand — MedicMind / OxbridgeMind / Study Mind]. I see [Student name] enquired about [product] — do you have a few minutes for a quick chat?
discovery: What year group is [Student name] in right now?
Have they sat any practice [UCAT / TMUA / ESAT / etc.] yet? What score are they targeting?
Which universities are top of the list?
What have you already tried — self-study, a textbook, another tutor?
Is there a deadline you're working back from?
Who else is involved in the decision — both parents, the student themselves?
What's the rough budget the family is comfortable with?
general.discoveryNote: Listen for what the family hasn't said: a child who hates the idea is a different sale to one driving it. Match your tone to whoever's leading the conversation.
general.transitionToPitch: Based on what you've told me, I'd suggest [recommendation]. Can I walk you through how that would work?
general.closeSoft: Shall I get the booking confirmation across to you today? I can hold the slot for 24 hours while you talk it over.
general.closeUrgency: We've got [X] confirmed students on the [date] cohort already — once it hits [Y], we close registrations. I'd hate for [Student name] to miss it.
general.closePriceAnchor: The standard rate is £30–40 per hour. With the complimentary hours I just mentioned, you're effectively at £[lower]. That's well below what most one-to-one providers charge.
general.followup: Thanks for your time today. I'll send the booking confirmation and a calendar invite for [Student name]'s first session within the hour. Anything else flags — text me directly on this number.

openerOptions: Hi, this is [Name] from MedicMind. I see [Student name] enquired about UCAT prep — do you have five minutes to talk through what they're looking for?
Hi [Parent name], it's [Name] at MedicMind, returning your enquiry about medical school prep. Have I caught you at a good time?
Hi, MedicMind here — I see [Student name] is thinking about medicine. Quick call to understand where they're at?
discoveryQuestions: What year is [Student name] currently in — Year 12 starting prep, or Year 13 already deep into it?
When are they planning to sit the UCAT?
What are their predicted A-levels? Specifically Chemistry and Biology?
Have they done any work experience yet — GP, hospital, hospice, care home?
Which med schools are top of the list? Different schools weight UCAT versus interview very differently.
Have they considered dentistry as a backup, or is it medicine only?
Where are they starting from on UCAT — have they sat a mock?

objections.objection: It's expensive.
objections.response: I hear you — and you're right that proper UCAT and interview prep isn't cheap. The way we frame it: a medicine application costs the family £127 for UCAS, around £200 for UCAT registration, then five years of student debt if they get in. The prep is the cheapest part of the chain that decides whether the rest happens at all. We also have a 12-month installment plan via GoCardless — 3% transaction fee, no interest, so it works out around £[X] a month.

objections.objection: We'll just buy the question bank and self-study.
objections.response: Honestly, that works for some students — usually the very disciplined ones already scoring 650+. For most students the difference is interpretation. The question bank tells you what you got wrong; a tutor tells you why you keep getting that pattern wrong. We can start with a 2-hour trial — money back if the family isn't happy.

objections.objection: My child doesn't want extra tutoring.
objections.response: That's actually quite common — and our tutors are used to it. Most are 22–28, recent medics themselves. They're not another teacher; they're someone who sat in this same chair four years ago and got in. The first session is usually about UCAT strategy rather than questions, which tends to land well.

objections.objection: We've already got a tutor.
objections.response: Brilliant — what are they working on? If it's general A-level support, that's not our market. If it's UCAT or interview specifically, who's the tutor and which med school did they get into? We're very specific about that — every UCAT tutor on our books scored top 10%.

objections.objection: Can the guarantee actually pay out?
objections.response: It can, but you're right to ask. It's Platinum tier only and the conditions are strict: every lesson attended, full UCAT question bank completed, every crash course attended, online courses finished, applied only to the universities we recommended, attended our consultation, and meeting minimum entry requirements. In practice most students don't meet every condition, which is why payouts are rare. I always frame it as a sales tool to commit them to the work, not a £500 windfall.

If they're buying UCAT only, ask about interview prep. Mention the interview handbook is free with any interview booking.
From 40 hours to Bronze Full Application: 'For 20 more hours you get all our crash courses, online courses, MMI circuits and the universities consultation. It's the whole prep year in one bundle.'
Gold → Platinum: lead with the Premium Tutor — top 1% of our pool, 1,000+ teaching hours. The £500 guarantee is the cherry on top, not the headline.

Our interview handbook usually retails at around £100 — it's free with any interview booking, including the smallest 5-hour package.

objections.objection: Dental schools are easier to get into than medical schools.
objections.response: Ratios are similar — about 6 applicants per place for both. Where dentistry differs is the interview: more practical, more reflective, less philosophical. Different prep, not less.

openerOptions: Hi, this is [Name] from OxbridgeMind. I see [Student name] is targeting Oxford / Cambridge for [subject] — happy to chat through prep?
Hi [Parent name], it's OxbridgeMind. Returning your enquiry about [subject] at Oxbridge.
discoveryQuestions: Is it Oxford, Cambridge, or both?
What subject are they applying for — and have they thought about which colleges?
Have they checked which entrance test their courses use — TMUA, ESAT, TARA, UCAT, LNAT?
What are their predicted grades? Most Oxbridge offers are A*AA or A*A*A.

objections.objection: Oxbridge tutoring is just paying for what you can get with reading lists.
objections.response: True for super-curricular reading itself. Not true for interview prep — Oxbridge interviews are deliberately disorienting, with leading questions and pivots designed to test how a student handles being wrong. You can't read your way through that; you have to practise it. That's what our tutors give them.

objections.objection: Aren't the new admissions tests (TMUA / ESAT / TARA) too new to prep for?
objections.response: They're new in name, but the question types are largely lifted from MAT, NSAA and TSA — which we've been teaching for years. Pearson VUE publishes specimen papers and we work through every one. We're not guessing; we know the format.

objections.objection: Why does Oxbridge need a different tutor to my A-level tutor?
objections.response: A-level rewards memorising the syllabus correctly. Oxbridge rewards going off-piste in a defensible way. Different skill. Most of our Oxbridge tutors are postgrads currently teaching at Oxford or Cambridge — they know what the admissions tutors actually look for.

objections.objection: The LNAT is just reading comprehension — why do I need a tutor?
objections.response: Section A is reading comprehension. Section B is a 750-word argumentative essay marked by Oxford and UCL admissions tutors directly. That's where the differentiation happens. We work on structure, signposting and the unspoken rules of what makes an LNAT essay feel competent.

objections.objection: Can my child just attend the Law Career Camp instead?
objections.response: The camp is a brilliant intensive — moot workshops, UK Supreme Court visit, mock trials with practising barristers, the LNAT workshop. It's not a substitute for 1-to-1 essay prep, but it's a fantastic complement. Many of our top-scoring LNAT students did both.

objections.objection: It's too expensive.
objections.response: I hear you. Compared to a UK-Oxbridge tutoring intensive (similar week, no residential) it actually comes out cheaper, and a chunk of it is the accommodation. We can also send a parent-friendly breakdown of what £1,799 actually buys — workshops, all meals, evenings out, 24/7 safeguarding, a Study Mind guardian living in the building.

objections.objection: Will my child make friends?
objections.response: It's the most common worry, and our strongest answer. They go out into London every evening with the guardians — bowling, mini golf, Covent Garden, family dinners with the founders. Cohorts are 5–10 students per subject. Last year's students are still in WhatsApp groups together a year on.

objections.objection: Is it safe?
objections.response: Students are never alone. 1 guardian per 10 students at all times. Ramsay Hall has 24/7 security on top of our guardians living in the building. Our guardians (Inga, Mariam and others) are specifically trained in safeguarding. Boys and girls are on separate floors.

objections.objection: What if my child has dietary requirements?
objections.response: Ramsay Hall covers vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, and most allergies as standard. Send us the specifics with the booking and we confirm with the kitchen before they arrive.

objections.objection: I don't want to commit until I know the timetable.

The structure is locked: it's the specific day-of-week within each week that can shift for industry guest availability.

commonObjections.q: We can just buy a Medify subscription for £150.
commonObjections.a: Medify gives you questions. It doesn't watch how you approach a question. Most students plateau around 600 on self-study — the breakthrough to 700+ usually needs a coach pointing out the timing or interpretation issue they can't see themselves.

commonObjections.q: Why does UCAT need 20+ hours?
commonObjections.a: Four sections, each with its own technique. Verbal Reasoning alone usually needs 6-8 hours to fix scanning speed. 20 hours is the minimum to cover all four sections properly; 40 hours is where serious score jumps happen.

commonObjections.q: My child has done UCAT prep already.
commonObjections.a: Brilliant — what score were they hitting? We're usually looking at a 100-point improvement from where students start with self-study. If they're already at 700+, we'd pitch fewer hours focused on the weakest section.

doNotSay: Don't claim every tutor scored 900+ — top 10% is the actual standard.

workshopDetails.Hospice: You'll understand the aims and principles of palliative care by spending the day with palliative doctors and nurses at North London Hospice (NLH).
workshopDetails.UCAT: Students are taken through the general structure of the UCAT exam and then will focus on each section in detail and receive specific exam technique guidance.
workshopDetails.Clinical Skills: Understand the complexities of the human body and the intricacies of medical care. Basic medical procedures and a thorough understanding of anatomy are indispensable, so this workshop aims to equip students with these core skills. Students will learn the general inspections of the hands, face, chest, and also palpate and ausculate.
workshopDetails.Laparoscopic Surgery: Students are introduced to the tools and techniques of camera supported minimally invasive surgery. They will gain experience with surgical cameras which support the work done in theatre rooms for patient operations.

workshopDetails.Solving Clinical Cases Workshop: This workshop teaches students how doctors actually think, moving them from textbook knowledge into real clinical reasoning. Students work through progressively harder cases, building a differential diagnosis, selecting investigations, and committing to a management plan. Cases span respiratory, abdominal, paediatric, and acute presentations, with the tutor drawing out cognitive pitfalls such as anchoring bias and premature closure. By the end, students can structure a history, justify a differential, and articulate their reasoning in the way medical school interviewers expect.
workshopDetails.History Taking: Learn how communication and teamwork are important in medicine and vital in history taking. Utilise effective verbal and non-verbal communication skills to facilitate smooth communication and develop good bedside manner. workshopDetails.Examinations: Utilise the information learnt from history taking to understand symptoms and causes for illnesses and injuries to support patient medical care
workshopDetails.Audiology and Tinnitus: This workshop offers a valuable opportunity to see how psychological principles are applied within an interdisciplinary healthcare context. Students will learn how CBT and related therapeutic techniques are incorporated into tinnitus treatment, how anxiety and attention can shape sensory experiences, and how mental-health interventions can significantly improve patient outcomes. By examining tinnitus through both a clinical and psychological lens, students gain practical insight into the mind–body connection and the role of psychology in managing complex health conditions.

workshopDetails.Medical Ethics: In this session, students explore the core principles of medical ethics, including autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. Medical ethics are vital to the welfare of patients and staff and supports decision-making in tough situations. Students will discuss prominent questions in this field and explore how to navigate a range of scenarios and topics.

workshopDetails.Introduction: Psychology: Discover the fascinating world of psychology through this dynamic workshop that explores the mind, behaviour, and human experience.
workshopDetails.Social Psychology: This session will allow for students to understand at a greater depth how humans functions in social groups and the unique phenomena that are developed through it. They will engage with percieved fundamental human social concepts such as altruism and conformity and see how such theories are utilised around the world in different contexts where there exists social group conflicts.
workshopDetails.Individual Psychology: This session offers a great opportunity for students to learn about the unique differences between people, in terms of the mind, and how they play out in the real world. They will learn about the wide variety of different markers of individuality such as personality differences and IQ and engage with the way they are understood in psychology as well as develop their own criticisms of such frameworks.

Through discussion and analysis of studies, studnets will learn how sleep affects memory, mood, and cognition, and examine the mechanisms that regulate our circadian rhythms. By the end, they will gain a deeper understanding of the vital role sleep plays in human health and behaviour.
workshopDetails.Drug addiction from a clinical perspecti: Students will focus on learning the effects and causes of different types of addiction - mainly drug addiction. They will look at this from different psychological lenses that ultimately make up the clinical lens, from a neuroscience point of view to a behavioural and cognitive point of view.
workshopDetails.Neuroplasticity: Neuroplasticity refers to the brain's ability to reorganise itself by forming new neural connections throughout life. This remarkable process allows the brain to adapt in response to learning, experiences, and even injury. During the session, students will explore the science behind neuroplasticity and how it can be harnessed to improve cognitive function, learning capabilities, and mental well-being. By understanding how the brain rewires itself, students will gain insights into enhancing their own brain health and resilience.
workshopDetails.Drama Therapy: In this workshop, students will observe Dr. Julianne Mullen, an experienced HCPC-registered Dramatherapist, as she demonstrates how drama therapy can support patients’ emotional and psychological wellbeing. Students will take part in a guided therapeutic exercise, gaining firsthand experience of how creative arts are integrated into the healing process. The session will also highlight the clinical connections between drama therapy and psychological treatment, offering insight into the evidence-based benefits of using creative approaches to support mental health and personal growth.
workshopDetails.Audiology and Tinnitus: This workshop offers a valuable opportunity to see how psychological principles are applied within an interdisciplinary healthcare context. Students will learn how CBT and related therapeutic techniques are incorporated into tinnitus treatment, how anxiety and attention can shape sensory experiences, and how mental-health interventions can significantly improve patient outcomes. By examining tinnitus through both a clinical and psychological lens, students gain practical insight into the mind–body connection and the role of psychology in managing complex health conditions.
workshopDetails.Experimental Research: This workshop introduces students to the design, methodology, and interpretation of experimental research in psychology. Participants will explore how controlled studies are used to investigate behaviour, cognition, and emotion, and will examine the challenges of creating valid, reliable, and ethically sound experiments. The session provides insight into how experimental research shapes psychological theory and informs evidence-based practice.
workshopDetails.Twist Museum Trip: This trip to the Twist Museum in London offers an immersive exploration of the psychology of perception, using illusions and interactive exhibits to reveal how the brain processes reality - building on what would be taught in the previous workshop. Students can investigate concepts such as depth, colour, size, and perspective, while reflecting on how our senses can be deceived. This engaging environment provides both an entertaining experience and a valuable academic insight into cognitive and perceptual psychology.
workshopDetails.Bethlem Museum Trip: In the Bethlem Museum of the Mind, set within the grounds of the historic Bethlem Royal Hospital, students will explore the rich and often challenging history of mental health care. Its collections include striking artworks created by former patients, alongside fascinating archives that trace changing ideas about the mind and its treatment. A visit offers students a powerful opportunity to reflect on the relationship between mental illness, creativity, and society’s evolving understanding of the human mind.
workshopDetails.Freud Museum London: Visiting the Freud Museum London, students will be offered an unparalleled insight into the intellectual world of Sigmund Freud, preserving his study, library, and the famous psychoanalytic couch where the foundations of modern psychotherapy were laid. Visitors encounter not only Freud’s extensive collection of antiquities but also the interdisciplinary influences - ranging from art to archaeology - that shaped his theories of the mind. For students, it provides a rare opportunity to critically engage with the origins of psychoanalysis and to consider its enduring impact on psychology, philosophy, and cultural thought.

workshopDetails.Intro to Higher Level Maths: Dive into higher mathematics beyond basic calculations. Learn what truly defines this field from renowned mathematicians, explore pure versus applied mathematics, and experience the mathematical thinking that drives innovation across science, technology, and philosophy.
workshopDetails.Understanding Infinity: Dive into the mind-bending concept of infinity, where we'll explore mathematical paradoxes and compare infinite quantities.
workshopDetails.Basics of Set Theory and Proofs: This workshop gives students a first look at set theory—the language of modern mathematics—covering sets, subsets, unions, intersections, and cardinality. Students will also be introduced to mathematical proofs, exploring direct proof, contradiction, and counterexamples. By the end, they will understand how sets and proofs form the foundation of higher-level mathematical thinking.
workshopDetails.Exploring Vector Spaces: This workshop introduces students to the fundamentals of vector spaces, including vectors, linear combinations, span, and bases. Through examples and problem-solving, students will see how these ideas extend beyond A-Level vectors into abstract structures. The session highlights the power of vector spaces as a foundation for linear algebra and its wide applications.
workshopDetails.Linear Algebra: This workshop demystifies the fascinating world of linear algebra by exploring vector spaces, their properties, and applications across multiple dimensions—essential knowledge for anyone pursuing STEM disciplines.
workshopDetails.College Level Maths: This workshop introduces Year 12 students to the world of higher mathematics, moving beyond A-Level into concepts like infinity, proofs, and linear algebra. Through interactive activities and group challenges, students explore both abstract and applied branches of maths. The session highlights how university-level maths emphasises reasoning, creativity, and real-world applications.
workshopDetails.Basics to Game Theory: In this session, we will introduce the foundational concepts of game theory, including players, strategies, payoffs, and the distinction between cooperative and non-cooperative games. We’ll explore classic examples like the Prisoner’s Dilemma and Nash Equilibrium, building intuition for strategic decision-making in competitive and cooperative settings
workshopDetails.Advanced Euclidean Geometry: We will delve into deeper results in Euclidean geometry, focusing on powerful tools such as homothety, inversion, and radical axes. We’ll work through elegant Olympiad-level problems to develop geometric intuition and explore the interplay between classical constructions and modern problem-solving techniques.
workshopDetails.Number Theory and Cryptography: We will explore key concepts in number theory such as divisibility, modular arithmetic, and prime numbers, laying the groundwork for understanding modern cryptographic systems. The session will then introduce classical encryption methods (like RSA) to show how number theory underpins secure communication in the digital world.
workshopDetails.An Introduction to Projective Geometry: This session introduces the fundamental ideas of projective geometry, beginning with the extension of the Euclidean plane to include points at infinity and the unification of parallel and intersecting lines. We'll cover key concepts such as homogeneous coordinates, the cross ratio, projective transformations, and duality. Classic theorems like Desargues' and Pappus’ will be explored both synthetically and algebraically to highlight the deep structure and surprising symmetries of projective space.
workshopDetails.Fundamental Multivariable Calculus: In this workshop, we will extend the ideas of single-variable calculus to functions of several variables, focusing on partial derivatives, gradients, and multiple integrals. We'll explore topics such as level sets, the Jacobian, and optimization with constraints using Lagrange multipliers, emphasizing both geometric understanding and computational techniques.
workshopDetails.A Brief History of Mathematics: This session offers a sweeping overview of the history of mathematics, tracing its development from ancient civilizations such as Babylon, Egypt, and Greece through to key milestones in Islamic, Indian, and European mathematics. We’ll highlight major breakthroughs—like the invention of zero, the development of calculus, and the rise of formal logic—while exploring how mathematical ideas evolved alongside culture, science, and philosophy.
workshopDetails.Topology: We will meet the core concepts of topology, focusing on open and closed sets, continuity, homeomorphisms, and basic topological spaces like the torus and Möbius strip. We’ll explore how topology studies the properties of space preserved under continuous deformations, and build intuition through visual examples, puzzles, and foundational theorems like the classification of surfaces and the notion of connectedness and compactness.
workshopDetails.Basics of Graph Theory: This session covers the fundamentals of graph theory, including vertices, edges, paths, cycles, and connectedness. We'll explore key concepts like trees, Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths, and basic applications in networks and combinatorics.
workshopDetails.Pure vs Applied Math: This workshop will explore the distinction between pure and applied mathematics, discussing how pure math focuses on abstract theory and structures while applied math tackles real-world problems through modeling and computation. We'll examine examples from both areas to highlight their different goals, methods, and how they often influence each other.
workshopDetails.MAT, STEP, TMUA: This session will introduce the MAT, STEP, and TMUA exams, focusing on their formats, question styles, and the mathematical thinking they test. We'll work through sample problems and strategies to help students build problem-solving skills and time management for these challenging university entrance assessments.
workshopDetails.London Academy of Trading: This exclusive visit to a premier trading institution offers students hands-on experience with professional traders, exposure to market analysis techniques, and insights into potential careers in financial markets through interactive trading simulations.

faq.question: Is there a payment plan?
faq.answer: Yes — 12 monthly installments via GoCardless. We add a 3% transaction fee to the total and split that across the 12 months. There's no interest. Never describe it as interest-bearing.

faq.question: Does the £500 money-back guarantee apply to Gold?
faq.answer: No. The guarantee is Platinum only. Conditions: all lessons attended, full UCAT question bank completed, all crash courses attended, online courses finished, applied to recommended universities, attended the consultation, and meets minimum entry requirements.

faq.question: Do you still offer BMAT prep?
faq.answer: No. BMAT has been discontinued. Don't pitch BMAT packages.

faq.question: Is the interview handbook included in a 5-hour interview booking?
faq.answer: Yes — it's free with any interview booking, no matter the size. Lead with this in the pitch.

faq.question: Does veterinary science need the UCAT?
faq.answer: No. Veterinary has no UCAT. Only Cambridge requires an entrance exam (ESAT). Oxford does not offer veterinary science. The Full Application Scheme is the right fit only for Cambridge vet applicants.

faq.question: Can a medicine tutor teach UCAT for a dentistry applicant?
faq.answer: Yes. UCAT is the same exam for medicine and dentistry. Only interviews and consultations need a specialist tutor.

faq.question: What's the difference between a crash course and a live day?
faq.answer: They're the same thing. Use 'live day' in operational copy; both terms are recognised by customers.

faq.question: Are the prices on this CRIB the official prices?
faq.answer: No — prices here lag the live website. Always confirm against the website before quoting a family.

faq.question: What admissions tests are still active for 2026 entry?
faq.answer: UCAT, TMUA, ESAT, TARA, LNAT, STEP, HUMAT. BMAT, MAT, PAT, MLAT, HAT, TSA, ENGAA, NSAA and others have been dropped or replaced. See the Taxonomy section.

faq.question: How does the Premium Tutor upgrade work?
faq.answer: Included in Platinum by default. Available on Bronze/Silver/Gold as a £5-per-hour upgrade on the full package. Confirm current rate before quoting.

faq.question: How many hours should I aim for on a UCAT-only sale?
faq.answer: 20 to 40 hours. Most common single sale lands around 30. Push to 40 with a complimentary hour and a UCAT Live Day freebie when budget allows.

salesTips.body: If a parent is dithering between Bronze and Gold, Silver is the honest answer. It's where most successful applicants land.

salesTips.body: There's no entrance exam to prep for. You'll look unprepared. Steer them to hourly packages focused on personal statement and interview.

salesTips.body: The guarantee is conditional and rarely paid out. The Premium Tutor is the daily upgrade families feel. Lead with that.

salesTips.title: Mention the installment plan when sticker shock hits
salesTips.body: If a parent flinches at the total, immediately mention the 12-month installment plan. 3% fee, no interest, monthly cost is suddenly manageable.

salesTips.title: Use complimentary hours before discounts
salesTips.body: Complimentary hours cost us £12.50–15 each but feel generous. £-discounts feel less generous and reduce our margin more. Always pick one lever, not both.

salesTips.body: Live days run regardless of single-customer signup. Adding one student is near-zero marginal cost. Lead with it for UCAT, Easter, and MMI live days.

salesTips.body: These CRIB prices lag the live website. Quote a range and follow up with the exact figure after the call.

salesTips.body: UK students need work experience. The Medicine camp is genuinely special — hospice, King's College Hospital simulations, MMI circuit, suturing. Most adults never see this content.

managerBrief.title: Brief for the manager (example — London circuit at Ark King Solomon Academy)
managerBrief.note: Use as a template. Replace venue, time, station count. Improve and add a Loom walkthrough when possible.
managerBrief.body:
Time: 10am – 2pm (manager arrives 9.15am · tutors 9.45am)
Venue: King Solomon Academy, Penfold Street, London, NW1 6RX

• 9.15am — please arrive and enter the room. Receipt attached in case of any issue; phone (ideally WhatsApp call) if you need help. Wi-Fi is available; find it and share with tutors.

• Set up the room: 8 stations, 3 chairs each (1 interviewer, 2 students).

• When tutors arrive, ask them to set up at their station. Remind them to have the station brief ready to show students during reading time (can show on laptop) and to fill out feedback forms during the station.

• Students arrive 10am. Either ask one tutor to wait at the front of the school until 10.10am or ask reception to direct students to the classroom.

• Read out the student codes and names. Tell students they must give their interviewer their code and name before the station starts.

• 8–9 station circuit; each station 22 minutes. Either announce the timings or play the timing video on the projector with speakers: https://youtu.be/cO6N_nIldmE (used at the UCL summer school).

• Half-way break: 10 minutes for tutors and students.

• End of circuit: thank students for attending. Optionally go round each tutor and ask for 30 seconds of feedback to the group on their station — what went well, what didn't.

• Finish the circuit.

checklist.phase: Pre-booking (as soon as 4+ students sign up)
items: Check signup count — if ≤3, hold; if >3, proceed.
Ask Dane to update event description in booking system.
Pick venue + classroom in Enni with appropriate capacity.
Submit booking request via Enni (Friday morning latest).
If submitting Friday: phone Schools Plus to fast-track.
Receive booking confirmation from Enni / Schools Plus.
Save confirmation receipt as PDF — needed for the lead on the day.
Recruit lead tutor (priority: previous lead per city).
Recruit regular tutors at 1 per 2 students ratio.
Confirm tutor wages: £60 standard, £90/£100 lead.
Confirm Wi-Fi password + tech requirements with venue.
Send students venue details + map link.
Create Tutors + Manager WhatsApp group; share booking confirmation.
Brief the lead on duties and pass them the student contact list.
Brief regular tutors (laptops, arrival 20m early, dress smart).
Create Students + Manager WhatsApp group; share lead tutor's number; reminder to direct general Qs to Medic Mind.
Confirm tutor attendance + lead's arrival plan.
Send the lead the timing video link if they want to play it on the projector.
Lead arrives 9.15-9.30am (30m early).
Tutors arrive 9.45am (15-20m early).
Students arrive 10am.
Run 8-9 stations × 22min + halfway 10m break.
End-of-circuit feedback round (30s per tutor).
Post-circuit: collect feedback forms; send tutors thanks; Lead reports back any issues to Medic Mind.

alerts: DO NOT share the Enni password outside the operations team. Rotate immediately if it leaks.
DO NOT promise students a specific tutor on the day — staffing can shift.
DO NOT book on a Saturday or Sunday expecting Schools Plus to respond — they are closed.
DO NOT under-book the room — when in doubt, choose larger capacity; MMI rotations need elbow room.
